summary: A supplied vector reconstruction of British Columbia Petroleum Corporation's curled-flame emblem and four-line name, after its 1982/83 and 1991/92 annual reports (Internet Archive microfiche). Two designs — the stacked logo and the emblem alone — each in black and white. The two scans are kept as the logos' downloads. See package-README.md, construction/ and review/comparison.webp.

assets.label: British Columbia Petroleum Corporation — Emblem and name
assets.dateNote: The report’s year, not an adoption date.
assets.notes: A curled flame — a drop whose tail turns into a ring — over “British Columbia Petroleum Corporation” on four lines, set right, in a heavy old-style serif, white on the black cover of the 1982/83 annual report.
assets.fidelityNote: A supplied reconstruction: the emblem is one compound shape of eight cubic curves and two straight edges, with a real opening; the wordmark is 17 drawn letterforms in the manner of Goudy Heavyface (an inference from their shapes), placed to the 1982/83 scan, its worn C completed from Columbia’s. Emblem overlap 94–96% with the two scans; lettering about 77%. Print colours are not known; black and white follow the monochrome scans.
